subject: chemistry
title: Electronic structure
key_idea: Electrons occupy the lowest available shells first. The shells hold 2, 8, 8 electrons for the first 20 elements. The number of outer-shell electrons gives the group, and the number of shells gives the period.

blocks.text: Electrons are arranged in shells, also called energy levels. This section covers the rules for filling them.

items.meaning: A region around the nucleus that holds electrons at a set distance from it.
The shell furthest from the nucleus that contains electrons.
How the electrons of an atom are arranged in shells, written as numbers such as 2,8,1.

items: Electrons fill the lowest available shell (the innermost) first.
The first shell holds up to 2 electrons.
The second shell holds up to 8 electrons.
The third shell holds up to 8 electrons for the first 20 elements.
A new shell starts only when the one before it is full.
Electronic structure is written with commas (2,8,1) or full stops (2.8.1). Both mean the same.

items.text: Sodium has atomic number 11, so 11 electrons.
2 in the first shell, 8 in the second, leaving 1.
The electronic structure is 2,8,1. In a diagram, draw 2, 8 and 1 electrons on three shells.

items: Fill the shells from the inside out: 2, then 8, then 8.
The numbers in the electronic structure add up to the atomic number of an atom.
Electronic structures can be written as numbers (2,8,1) or drawn as a diagram.

blocks.text: An element's position in the periodic table follows from its electronic structure.

items: The number of electrons in the outer shell is the **group** number.
The number of occupied shells is the **period** number.
The elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic number, not atomic mass.
Elements in the same group have the same number of outer-shell electrons, so they react in similar ways.
Group 0 elements have a full outer shell.

diagram.alt: Pick an element to see its electronic structure, group and period.

items.text: The last number is 7, so 7 electrons in the outer shell: Group 7.
There are 3 numbers, so 3 shells are occupied: Period 3.

items: Group number = number of electrons in the outer shell.
Period number = number of shells with electrons in.
Use the numbers in your answer: for example, 7 electrons in the outer shell, so Group 7.

checks.q: Write the electronic structure of an atom of magnesium (atomic number 12).
An element has the electronic structure 2,8,3. State its group and period and explain your answer.
checks.a: Group 3, because it has 3 electrons in its outer shell. Period 3, because it has 3 shells occupied.

checks.q: State one difference and one similarity in the electronic structures of sodium (2,8,1) and chlorine (2,8,7).
checks.a: Difference: sodium has 1 outer-shell electron and chlorine has 7. Similarity: both have 3 shells (both are in Period 3).

exam_phrases: sodium has one and chlorine has seven electrons in the outer shell

mistakes.wrong: Sodium has seven electrons in its outer shell.
mistakes.right: Sodium has one and chlorine has seven. If you quote a number of electrons it must be correct, or the mark is lost.

mistakes.wrong: The electronic structure of potassium is 2,8,9.
mistakes.right: The third shell holds 8 electrons before a fourth shell starts. Potassium is 2,8,8,1.

worked_example.question:
This question is about sodium and chlorine.

State one difference and one similarity in the electronic structure of sodium and of chlorine.
answer_points: Difference: sodium has one electron in its outer shell and chlorine has seven.
Similarity: both have three shells (levels), or both have electrons in the third shell, or both have incomplete outer shells.
Both have 2 electrons in the inner shell, or both have 8 electrons in the second shell, is also accepted.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the difference and one for the similarity. Any number of electrons you quote must be correct.

exam_phrases: 1 electron in the outer shell (so group 1)
number of electrons in the outer shell gives the group number
number of electron shells gives the period number
3 shells / 3 numbers in the electronic configuration, so period 3

mistakes.wrong: Chlorine has 3 outer shells, so it is in period 3.
mistakes.right: The answer '3 outer shells' is rejected. Say chlorine has 3 shells, so it is in period 3.

mistakes.wrong: Group 1 metals have 1 electron in their atom.
mistakes.right: State 1 electron in the outer shell. The second mark depends on getting the first right, and an incorrect number of electrons is rejected.

worked_example.question:
This question is about potassium and zinc.

Explain how the electronic configuration of an atom of potassium is related to its position in the periodic table.
answer_points: The number of electrons in the outer shell gives the group number: 1 electron in the outer shell, so Group 1.
The number of electron shells gives the period number: 4 shells, so Period 4.
worked_example.tip: Link each part of the structure to its position, using the numbers for potassium (2.8.8.1).

exam_phrases: group 7 as 7 electrons in the outer shell
in order of increasing atomic number / proton number

mistakes.wrong: The elements in the periodic table are in order of atomic mass.
mistakes.right: Atomic mass is not allowed. The elements are in order of increasing atomic number (proton number).
A bare position scores only the position marks. Each needs its reason: 7 electrons in the outer shell, and 3 shells occupied.

worked_example.question:
Element C has the electronic structure 2.8.7.

What does this tell you about the position of element C in the periodic table?

Explain your answer.
answer_points: Because it has 7 electrons in its outer shell.
worked_example.tip: Two marks for the position (group and period) and two for the reasons. Give each reason with its number.
